title: All-electrical Coherent Control of a Single Rare-earth Spin Qubit
authors: Yaowu Liu, Dasom Choi, Stefano Reale, Jeongmin Oh, Seorhin Choi, Lei Fang, We-hyo Soe, Arzhang Ardavan, Andreas J. Heinrich, Soo-hyon Phark, Fabio Donati
abstract: Electrical control of single spin qubits is a major frontier for nanoscale, high-speed, and scalable quantum devices. Yet, extending it to highly shielded rare-earth 4f electrons remains an experimental challenge across solid-state platforms. Here we demonstrate all-electrical coherent control of a single Er electron spin, which is exchange-coupled to a nearby Ti atom. Scanning tunneling microscopy-based electron spin resonance with three-dimensional magnetic-field control enables comprehensive mapping of the resonance and Rabi frequencies, revealing pronounced anisotropies in both the Er g-tensor and the Er-Ti exchange interaction. The electrical modulation of the anisotropic Er-Ti coupling results in an efficient drive of the Er spin, allowing us to achieve near-gigahertz Rabi frequencies - a ten-fold improvement over the present record for rare-earth spin qubits. By establishing anisotropic exchange as a general resource for electrically accessing shielded rare-earth spins, our results open a new route to ultrafast and local control of rare-earth spins in solid-state quantum devices.
summary: The paper reports on achieving all-electrical coherent control of a single rare-earth spin qubit using an Er-Ti pair system. By utilizing the anisotropy in the spin-spin exchange coupling, they achieved record high Rabi frequencies (near GHz) for the Er spin transition. This work opens a new route for ultrafast local control of challenging solid-state quantum systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving all-electrical coherent control of single rare-earth (Er) spin qubits due to the strong shielding of their 4f electrons.
main_result: The authors demonstrated all-electrical coherent control, achieving near-gigahertz Rabi frequencies for the Er spin transition—a ten-fold improvement over previous records. This establishes anisotropic exchange as a general resource for ultrafast control in solid-state quantum devices.
method: Scanning tunneling microscopy (STM)-based electron spin resonance (ESR) spectroscopy combined with three-dimensional magnetic-field control was used to map resonance and Rabi frequencies.
model_or_system: The system involves an Er-Ti spin pair adsorbed on a surface, modeled by a spin Hamiltonian incorporating exchange and dipolar interactions. The coherent drive is achieved by electrically modulating the anisotropic Er-Ti coupling.
key_observables: Resonance and Rabi frequencies for various transitions ($f_1$ to $f_5$), anisotropy in the Er g-tensor and Er-Ti exchange interaction, and the dependence of these on external magnetic field angles ($	heta$).
important_parameters: Near-gigahertz Rabi frequencies; linear scaling of Rabi frequencies with applied RF voltage ($V_{RF}$); anisotropic coupling strength $J$.
main_assumptions: The mechanism relies on transducing electrical excitations into an effective transverse driving field ($B_1$) via the anisotropic exchange interaction.
figures_summary: Figures show ESR transitions and Rabi oscillations confirming high efficiency on the Er spin, comparing results across different atomic separations/orientations, and mapping angular dependencies of these frequencies.
paper_structure: The work progresses from demonstrating basic all-electrical control to detailed characterization using Hamiltonian modeling. It maps out anisotropies in g-tensors and exchange coupling, culminating in a general mechanism for ultrafast spin manipulation via anisotropic exchange modulation.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the physical realization of solid-state qubits by providing an electrical pathway (via anisotropic exchange) to manipulate highly shielded spins, which is crucial for scalable quantum computing architectures.
